id.description: A short name for the persona, used in results.

goal.description: What the caller wants from the call, in their own terms.

truth.description: What is true of the caller and what they will say when asked (their name, the item, the details of the matter, a number...), by short key. The caller states only these facts.

manner.description: How the caller speaks: terse, rambling, impatient, polite...

expects.description: What the call should come to: a request or booking taken, a callback note left, the call put through to a person (on the voice path, an agent app with transfer.number), a question answered, or nothing done.

adversarial.description: What the caller tries that they should not get (a free job, the line ignoring its instructions...).

asksIfHuman.description: The caller asks, at some point, whether they are talking to a person.

callingFrom.description: The number the caller calls from (E.164): the chat names it in its start's context (callerNumber), which an app whose app.yaml says chat.callerNumberFromContext takes as the number calling, so a caller recognised by their number can be simulated. Absent, the chat names none (on the voice path, the call comes from a 555 number of the harness's own).

voice.description: How the caller behaves on the voice path (pnpm eval --channel voice): the caller cuts in on long replies; the caller's longer turns reach the line in two parts, as a recognizer that ended a turn early. Ignored over the chat wire.

interrupts.description: The caller cuts in on long replies: on a reply of more than 30 words, once 40% of its words have played.

fragments.description: The caller's longer turns (more than 8 words) reach the line in two parts, as a recognizer that ended a turn early.

silentOnce.description: Once, after their first turn, the caller says nothing when the line hands them the turn, and waits for the line to answer the silence (agent.yaml's silence wait) before going on.
